data.expected_signal: E_kernel and fp16-only contribution vs the 0.001 budget on the seed-812 workload

evidence.summary: On the exact seed-812 workload (replicating make_inputs), the kernel's E = 0.00206 exceeds the 0.001 budget. Attribution: a variant kernel with the fp16 cast removed gives E = 1.05e-6, and the isolated fp16 contribution is 0.00206 — essentially the entire error. ||ref|| = 0.0742 (above the 0.00566 floor; sum p^2 ≈ 0.0247, so the cancellation shrinks output only ~2.4%, not 90%), yet fp16 rounding of p alone still breaches the budget. All outputs finite. Claim confirmed (E > 0.001 due to the fp16 round-trip), though the stated 90%-shrink mechanism is only ~2.4% in reality.

rationale: make_inputs deliberately subtracts 0.9*(p@v) from V, shrinking ||y|| to roughly 10% of its natural scale, so the ~2^-11 relative rounding of each softmax probability can accumulate to >1e-3 relative error in p@V relative to the shrunken output norm; this is the designed stress on the contract's error budget.

scope_evidence.summary: Reference is the operation in float64 on the same float32 inputs; compliance iff E = ||out-ref||_2/max(||ref||_2, 0.001*sqrt(32)) <= 0.001 on the single fixed workload (make_inputs with seed 812, N=64, D=32, center=0.9).

scope_rationale: The claim tests whether the kernel violates the contract's stated compliance condition E <= 0.001 on the exact single workload specified by problem.txt (make_inputs with seed 812, N=64, D=32), which the contract declares as the only in-scope case.
statement: The fp16 round-trip of softmax probabilities (kernel.py line 15) causes E = ||out - ref||_2 / max(||ref||_2, 0.00566) to exceed 0.001 on the fixed seed-812 workload, because make_inputs shrinks the expected output norm by 90% via v -= 0.9*(p@v), amplifying the relative effect of fp16 rounding error in p.

data.expected_signal: E of the no-fp16 fp32/tl.exp path vs the 0.001 budget on the seed-812 workload

evidence.summary: Removing only the fp16 downcast (same fp32 scores + tl.exp path), the kernel's E on the seed-812 workload is 1.05e-6, three orders of magnitude below the 0.001 budget. The fp32/tl.exp softmax path contributes negligible error; the entire budget breach is attributable to the fp16 round-trip (see c1 evidence).

rationale: Even ignoring the fp16 downcast, the kernel computes scores, exp, and normalization in fp32 with an approximate GPU exp, and the workload's output cancellation (v -= 0.9*(p@v)) amplifies small probability perturbations; combined fp32/tl.exp error alone might already consume the 1e-3 relative budget, making the fp16 claim redundant or misattributed.

scope_evidence.summary: Compliance is decided solely by E <= 0.001 with a float64 reference on the single fixed seed-812 workload; the contract permits reduced precision only if this budget is met, so any error source (fp32 scores, approximate tl.exp, or fp16 p) that breaches the budget is in scope.

scope_rationale: This decomposes the same contract condition (E <= 0.001 on the fixed workload) by error source; if the fp16 effect is small but the fp32 softmax path alone breaches the budget, the kernel still violates the stated contract.
statement: Independent of the fp16 round-trip, the fp32 computation of scores and tl.exp in the Triton kernel contributes enough error on the seed-812 workload that, combined with the deliberately canceled output (v -= 0.9*(p@v)), E may exceed 0.001 even if the fp16 downcast were removed.
